guardrails.description: Layer-4 (judge_online) evaluators that run inline on every /invoke. Each entry must declare 'timeout_ms' (how long the evaluator may run before the proxy aborts it) and 'on_timeout' (fail_open releases the request, fail_closed blocks). Both knobs are required - guardrails sit on the production hot path and the fail-mode is too consequential to default. Entry type is resolved via the 'guardrail.<type>' entry-point name.

gates.description: Legacy global gates. Per-layer gates under top-level 'layers' supersede this; both shapes are accepted simultaneously.

run_mode.description: Layer-interaction policy. 'always' runs every layer; 'short_circuit' aborts on any layer fail; 'short_circuit_blocking_only' (default) skips later layers only when an upstream block-severity gate fails.

layers.description: Per-layer gates. Keys are stable layer names: heuristics, metrics, judge_offline, judge_online, human.

retry.description: Run-wide default retry policy for provider calls. Per-provider overrides live under each provider's ``config.retry``. Retry is bounded exponential backoff with jitter; ``retry_on`` is a list of regex patterns matched (case-insensitively) against ``f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}'``.

systems.description: External systems referenced by evaluators (e.g. databases for the text_to_sql template). Values support ${ENV} substitution so secrets stay out of the repo. Each entry is a free-form object the consuming evaluator interprets — schema validation only enforces 'an object keyed by id'.

kind.description: Free-text label for the system kind, e.g. 'postgres', 'shadow_sqlite', 'snowflake'.

gate_strategy.description: How to combine per-trial gate verdicts. 'all' (default) requires every trial to pass all blocking gates; 'any' passes the run if at least one trial passes.

audit.description: Per-run audit / governance controls. Events are always recorded; this block configures retention and privacy.

redact_payload.description: When true, strip rendered prompts / raw responses / judge reasons from event payloads but keep their content hashes so the chain still verifies.

refusal_response.description: How the proxy returns when a layer-4 guardrail with mode=block refuses a response. 'mode' has no default - the choice between an HTTP-honest refusal and a chatbot-friendly 200 is too consequential to pick for the operator. Required as soon as any 'guardrails:' evaluator is configured.

mode.description: 'http_error' returns HTTP 'status' (default 403) with the reason in the body; raw API consumers handle this as a typed error. 'http_200_refusal' returns 200 with the configured 'text' in the response 'output' field and 'blocked_by' populated; chatbot UIs render this as a polite refusal turn.

status.description: Only used when mode == 'http_error'. 403 Forbidden is the default; 451 (legal) is the standards-aligned alternative for policy refusals.

text.default: This response was blocked by the project's guardrail policy.
text.description: Human-readable refusal string. Used as the response 'output' when mode == 'http_200_refusal' and as the body 'detail' when mode == 'http_error'.

mode.description: Inline-gate dispatch policy used by the layer-4 'judge_online' guardrail on the /invoke path. 'block' refuses the response per the project's 'refusal_response' config; 'warn' annotates the row as failed without blocking; 'log' records the verdict without changing the response. Parallel to 'severity' (which drives batch-shape gate verdicts on completed runs).

timeout_ms.description: Per-evaluator timeout for inline (layer-4) dispatch. Falls back to each evaluator's own 'timeout_ms' when set there; this is the layer-wide default.

on_timeout.description: What to do when an inline evaluator hits 'timeout_ms'. 'fail_open' lets the request through (industry-standard for inline guardrails - don't degrade live traffic on a guardrail outage). 'fail_closed' refuses per 'mode'. No default - the policy is too consequential to pick for the operator.

evaluator.description: Optional: scope this gate to a single evaluator id rather than the layer roll-up.

min_delta_vs_baseline.description: When ``type: relative`` and a baseline file is provided, the gate fails if (actual − baseline_actual) < min_delta_vs_baseline.

max_delta_vs_baseline.description: Symmetric to min_delta_vs_baseline; useful for cost / latency gates that should not regress upward.

alternative.description: ``type: ttest`` directionality. Default ``less`` (regression-detection: fail when current is significantly lower than baseline).

min_n.description: ``type: ttest`` minimum sample size on each side. Below this, the gate skips non-blockingly. Default is 10 — Welch's t-test with df≈1 has too little power to be useful for regression detection. The schema accepts as low as 2 so test fixtures can opt down explicitly; production gates should keep the default or raise it.

custom_check.description: Escape hatch: invoke a Python function as part of this gate. Function signature: (metrics: dict, config: dict) -> {'passed': bool, 'details': list}.

module.description: Dotted path with optional ':' separator, e.g. 'my_pkg.gates:safety_check' or 'my_pkg.gates.safety_check'.
